summary: This original learning guide supports close study of “lwfÙkQlq/k 9 f}rh;% ikB% lwfDrlq/k” in Bhaswati / Sanskrit textbook — Part I. Read the complete selection in the supplied textbook before using the questions. Identify the speaker or narrator where relevant, the situation, key ideas, structure, language choices and any change in tone or viewpoint. Support interpretations with short references to the text; do not assume a theme or plot detail without checking the actual selection. For language-learning tasks, notice how vocabulary and sentence structure create meaning.

concepts.title: Read for meaning before interpretation
concepts.explanation: Identify who is speaking or narrating, what situation is presented, what changes and which details are emphasised. Separate explicit information from inference.
concepts.example: Write one sentence describing what the text directly says and a second sentence explaining what you infer from it.

concepts.title: Language choices create effects
concepts.explanation: Word choice, imagery, repetition, contrast, sentence length and structure can shape tone and emphasis. Explain the effect of a feature instead of merely naming it.
concepts.example: Choose one word or phrase from the text and explain how its connotations contribute to mood or meaning.

concepts.title: Support an interpretation
concepts.explanation: A defensible interpretation answers the question and is supported by relevant textual evidence. Different readings may be possible, but they should fit the text.
concepts.example: Make a claim about a character, idea or speaker, cite a relevant moment, then explain the connection.

concepts.title: Write clearly in your own words
concepts.explanation: A good response is organised, precise and relevant. Paraphrase ideas accurately and use quotations only when needed to support a point.
concepts.example: Use the sequence point → textual evidence → explanation, then link back to the question.

workedExamples.question: How can you analyse a passage from “lwfÙkQlq/k 9 f}rh;% ikB% lwfDrlq/k” without merely retelling it?
steps: State the passage’s situation or main idea in one sentence.
Choose a specific word, image, action or structural feature.
Explain the effect or implication of that feature.
Connect the interpretation to the question and support it with the text.
workedExamples.answer: Analysis explains how the text creates meaning; retelling only repeats what happens.

workedExamples.question: How should you answer a vocabulary-in-context question?
steps: Read the complete sentence and the surrounding lines.
Identify the part of speech and the sense that fits the context.
Replace the word with a possible synonym and check whether the sentence still makes sense.
workedExamples.answer: Use the meaning that fits the context, not simply the first dictionary meaning.

practice.question: Write a two-sentence summary of “lwfÙkQlq/k 9 f}rh;% ikB% lwfDrlq/k” after reading the original selection.
practice.answer: Sentence 1 should state the main situation or idea; sentence 2 should state its important development or implication. Fill this in only after reading the PDF.
practice.why: This prevents an invented summary from replacing the source text.

practice.question: Choose one textual detail that supports an interpretation. What should you explain?
practice.answer: Explain what the detail shows and how it supports the interpretation; do not leave the quotation unexplained.
practice.why: Evidence is persuasive only when its relevance is made clear.

practice.question: What is the difference between tone and topic?
practice.answer: The topic is what the text is about; tone is the attitude or manner conveyed by the language.
practice.why: A text can address one topic in different tones.

practice.question: How can you improve a written answer before submitting it?
practice.answer: Check relevance to the question, organisation, evidence, grammar, spelling and whether each point is explained.
practice.why: Revision improves clarity and prevents unsupported statements.

mcqs.q: A text-based interpretation should be supported by…
options: a plot detail not present in the text
mcqs.why: Interpretations should fit the actual text.

mcqs.q: The topic of a passage is…
options: the attitude conveyed by the speaker
mcqs.why: Topic refers to the subject; tone refers to attitude or manner.

mcqs.q: Tone is most directly shaped by…
options: the length of the title only
mcqs.why: Word choice and structure contribute to tone.

options: make a point, use evidence and explain it
mcqs.why: The evidence must be connected to the point.

mcqs.q: When the title alone does not establish a plot detail, the learner should…
options: read the selection and verify it
mcqs.why: The actual textbook selection is the authority for its content.
